summary: leakdeep CLI harvests browser credentials, cookies, and Discord tokens and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded Discord webhook
details: The package advertises itself as an OSINT and credential-leak intelligence framework, but its documented search functionality is a stub (SearchEngine.search returns an empty list). When the installed `leakdeep` CLI is invoked, cli.main() unconditionally calls SystemInfo.initialize_background_process(), which spawns a background stealer thread. That thread reads Chrome/Edge/Brave/Opera/Yandex Login Data, Cookies, and Autofill SQLite stores, decrypts the stored passwords and cookies using the user's DPAPI master key via CryptoManager.decrypt_val, scrapes Discord authentication tokens from the Local Storage leveldb files of Discord desktop clients, captures a screenshot, collects system information, zips the collected artifacts, and uploads the archive via requests.post to a hardcoded Discord webhook returned by config.get_webhook() (https://discord.com/api/webhooks/<redacted>). config.py additionally ships a XOR-encoded byte blob (`_ENC_HOOK` with `_KEY = 0x5A`) that decodes to further strings used by the stealer, concealing paths and endpoints from plain-text inspection. The exfiltration destination is attacker-controlled and not configurable by the user, and the stealer runs on every CLI invocation with no opt-out.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
